item.title: Fix window.py bug so python3 -m unittest passes
item.brief:
Operator request, verbatim: "In this repository `python3 -m unittest` fails. Find and fix the bug in `window.py` so every test passes, without changing the tests, and make sure the function is correct for every input, not just the tested ones. Commit your fix."

Goal: `python3 -m unittest` passes from the repository root.

Constraints:
- Do not modify any test files. Fix the bug in `window.py` only, unless the root cause is provably elsewhere and the change is minimal.
- The fix must be correct for all inputs the function accepts (including empty input, boundary sizes, and edge cases), not only the cases the tests cover. Reason about the boundaries explicitly and check them.
- Keep the change minimal and readable; add no unnecessary abstractions or comments.
- Commit the fix on the item's branch with a clear message describing the bug. Do not add any AI-generated attribution or co-author lines. Use the repository's existing git identity with no overrides.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `python3 -m unittest` exits 0 with all tests passing.
2. The test files are byte-identical to the base commit.
3. The fix is committed.

model_reasons.implement: Off-by-one style bug in one function; the brief asks for correctness on all inputs, so a stronger effort than the routine default is reasonable.

state.summary:
Fixed the off-by-one in window.py: sliding_windows used range(len(items) - size), which dropped the final window and returned [] when len == size. It now uses range(len(items) - size + 1). Committed as 6e76023 (tree 86fa257) on archon/pcfma761-fix-window-py-bug-so-python3-m-unittest, with no attribution lines. Checks: python3 -m unittest failed before the fix (failures=2) and now runs 3 tests, OK, exit 0. A brute-force sweep (lengths 0-7, sizes 1-9) matches a reference implementation. test_window.py is identical to base a0837e1. One reviewer (agt_01M8GMPGP6KZ24J48AEX42ZEFC, low effort, the diff is one line) passed the head with risk low. No processes left running. Open: I added no extra asserts, since the change is minimal and the existing ValueError guard covers the one invalid input; the repo has no contributor guidance file.

pr.body:
Approach: the start-index range stopped one short. Changed range(len(items) - size) to range(len(items) - size + 1) in window.py. Only one file changed; no test files touched.

Boundaries: empty list returns []; size == len gives one window; size > len gives []; size 1 gives len items; size <= 0 still raises ValueError.

Checks: python3 -m unittest before fix FAILED (failures=2); after fix Ran 3 tests OK exit 0. Brute-force sweep (len 0-7, size 1-9) against a reference implementation passed. test_window.py identical to base a0837e1.

Assumptions: no contributor guidance file exists in the repo; the function's existing ValueError guard is its validation, so no extra assertions were added to keep the change minimal.
pr.summary: made sliding_windows return the final window. now python3 -m unittest passes. before: range(len(items) - size) dropped last window and returned [] when len == size; now: range(len(items) - size + 1).
pr.title: Fix off-by-one that dropped the last sliding window
